verdict.reasoning: The doctor notes, "you're feeling hot. But you didn't mention that. Is that correct?" and the patient does not affirm feeling hot; instead he clarifies he feels short of breath. Thus feeling hot is not reported by the patient.
The doctor opens with "you are feeling hot and have had severe headaches. Is that correct?" and the patient replies "Yeah, it's really affecting my work," confirming severe headaches.

Patient: "One thing that's kind of weird is I sometimes also get some tingling in my arms" and later clarifies "Both" when asked if it is in one hand or both, indicating intermittent tingling in both arms.
Patient: "I kind of have. My heart is beating kind of fast" and later confirms noticing his heart beating, consistent with palpitations.
Patient: "I kind of lose my appetite also," indicating decreased appetite.
Patient: "I get this, like, feeling of, like, short breath. Sometimes" and confirms shortness of breath while sitting at his desk, indicating intermittent shortness of breath.
Patient: "There's one more thing that I think I should mention. Like, I do have, like, some loss of libido at home," confirming decreased libido.
Patient: "But it's started roughly when I changed jobs" and later confirms he is a lawyer at a law firm, tying symptom onset to the job change.

Patient: "Not really, but generally during work times" and "I get it mostly when I'm at work"; about location: "No, it's mostly in the front," supporting headaches primarily at work and in the front of the head.
When asked if he feels sick with the headache, patient says, "Not. Not really, but it's, like, making it hard. Yeah, I kind of feel a little bit nauseous, maybe," consistent with mild nausea.
Patient describes tingling as "Prickling? Yeah" and confirms it is in "Both" hands and "No" in legs, matching prickling tingling in both arms without leg involvement.
Regarding heart beating fast, patient says, "it's maybe once a day, maybe more," consistent with palpitations about once per day.

Doctor: "So do you feel short of breath while you're sitting at your desk?" Patient: "Yeah. No. Yes. Sorry. Yeah." and then "And how about when you're exercising?" Patient: "No." This supports SOB at the desk but not on exertion.
When asked about weight loss, patient answers "5Lbs" and confirms it is "not intentional," indicating unintentional 5‑pound weight loss.
To "have you noticed your clothes feeling looser?" patient says "Not really. No." and to "have people said or commented that you've lost weight?" he answers "No," matching the statement.
Loss of libido: Patient says it has been happening "Same amount of time. Really? Like, since I changed my job," confirming decreased libido since job change.
Patient: "Well, I have a hypothyroidism," clearly documenting hypothyroidism.
When asked about medication, patient answers "Thyroxine" and confirms "Yes" to remembering to take medications, indicating thyroxine use with adherence.
Doctor: "And are you allergic to anything?" Patient: "No." This supports no known allergies.
Patient: "I'm a lawyer." and to "do you work in London at the moment?" responds "Yes," confirming he works as a lawyer in London.
Doctor asks stress rating; patient: "I think it's seven or eight," indicating work stress of 7–8/10.
On alcohol: Patient: "Like once a week. A couple of glasses. One." which corresponds to about once per week, 1–2 glasses.
On smoking: Doctor: "And how about smoking?" Patient: "No." confirming he does not smoke.
Doctor asks about recreational drugs including cocaine or marijuana; patient answers "No" to both, indicating denial of illicit drug use.

The doctor explores headaches at work and stress (stress rated 7–8/10) and summarizes that "you've told me lots of things happening" without specifying another organic cause; describing them as workplace-related with a possible stress component is a reasonable direct inference from the history.

Doctor explicitly notes and explores new tingling: "And another thing that you also mentioned is that you notice tingling in your hand... And again, is this the first time you've noticed this?" Patient: "Yeah." This reflects assessment of new-onset paraesthesias in both arms.
The doctor questions and records both shortness of breath and awareness of heart beating fast, then plans heart and breathing checks, indicating assessment of palpitations and intermittent SOB.
Doctor specifically asks about reduced appetite and weight loss, quantifies "5Lbs" and confirms it is "not intentional," showing assessment of unintentional weight loss and decreased appetite.
The doctor acknowledges the patient's report of "some loss of libido" by asking "How long has that been happening for?" indicating active assessment of decreased libido.

Doctor reviews hypothyroidism and thyroxine adherence ("And do you take medications for that?" "Thyroxine." "And are you Remembering to take your medications?" "Yes."), suggesting hypothyroidism is considered stable on medication.
Doctor: "I think the best course of action is you come and see one of our doctors in the clinic. We can give you an examination," clearly arranging in‑person review.
Doctor: "and probably do some blood tests for your thyroxin," implying ordering blood tests including thyroid function.
Doctor: "we check your heart and your breathing, make sure that those things are functioning correctly," which describes performing cardiac and respiratory examination in clinic.
Doctor: "I think before we give you any medications, we should see you in person," implying no new medications now and monitoring until in‑person review.
Doctor: "I think you can book an appointment through the app to come and see clinic, see one of my colleagues," specifying booking via the app.

The encounter is by phone/video ("Can I check your name and date of birth, please?" and instructions to book in‑clinic for examination); there is no physical exam documented, consistent with no physical exam due to telehealth format.
